source_spans.name: fa_loader_selector
source_spans.description: Shared F9/FA loader selector; includes the branch to $9071/$9076 and the distinct post-helper $9FA8(A=$01) at $8BAE.

source_spans.name: clear_helper_entrypoints
source_spans.description: $9071 selects $2000; $9076 selects $2400; both configure 16 rows x 32 bytes and jump to $98E8.

source_spans.name: clear_row_producer
source_spans.description: $98E8 selects buffered rows when $4A|$4B is nonzero, reserves each row via $9B28, appends 32 zero bytes, finalizes, and increments destination by $20.

source_spans.name: queue_capacity_writer
source_spans.description: $9B28 tests queue cursor $0628 plus payload size against $3D, yields through $9FA8(A=$01), then writes a 3-byte header and payload; $9B5E finalizes the queue cursor.

source_spans.name: scene_56_fa_0f_event
source_spans.description: Scene-$56 background event operand; event stream begins at $BFBA with F1 $02 followed by FA $0F.

source_spans.name: background_0f_descriptor
source_spans.description: The bank-$07 descriptor selected by FA $0F; included as a source identity check, not used to invent a preclear destination.

decoded_rules.buffered_branch: $98E8 uses the buffered queue when ($4A | $4B) != 0; direct PPU writes are outside this task.
decoded_rules.queue_capacity: Before each row, $9B28 yields when $0628 + payload_size >= $3D; payload_size is 32. The byte comparison excludes the 3-byte queue header.
decoded_rules.queue_serialization: A successful row uses 3 queue header bytes plus 32 zero payload bytes; $9B5E records the cursor. A source-valid end cursor can therefore be as high as $3F.
decoded_rules.yield: $9B2E loads $01 and $9B30 calls $9FA8; $9B32 is the saved return word and $9B33 the resumed PC.
decoded_rules.queue_release_consumer_pc: $A03C (counted $05E8 queue writer loop); receipt PC must match exactly.
decoded_rules.post_helper_wait: $8BAE's separate LDA #$01 / JSR $9FA8 is outside this row task.

resource.byte_identity: Concatenated unchanged ROM source spans in manifest order.

runtime_policy.trace_role: Retained RAM frames validate route-level wait-state observations only; they do not seed runtime cursor, destination, or frame delays.
